def-qa-11-marked-search-problem:
## Definition

Fix an integer $n\ge0$, put $N=2^n$, and let $D_n=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$. The big-endian encoding $\operatorname{enc}_n:\{0,1\}^n\to D_n$ is a bijection by [[thm-qc-bitstring-index-is-bijection]], so identify each address word $w$ with its slot $x=\operatorname{enc}_n(w)$. A search instance is a total Boolean function $f:D_n\to\{0,1\}$, equivalently the word-indexed function $w\mapsto f(\operatorname{enc}_n(w))$. Its marked set is $M=\{x\in D_n:f(x)=1\}$ and its marked count is $t=|M|$. The standard bit query is the coherent XOR action $U_f|x,b\rangle=|x,b\oplus f(x)\rangle$; the associated phase query is $O_M|x\rangle=(-1)^{f(x)}|x\rangle$. One standard bit query implements this phase action with a response qubit prepared in $|-\rangle$, by [[thm-qa-bit-query-to-phase-query]]. A measured candidate $x$ is verified by a separate standard bit query. Knowing $t$ is additional classical input; no count promise is made in the unknown-count version. A correct search output is a verified $x\in M$. The distinguished output none is used only by a procedure whose input includes the exact fact $t=0$; it is not a finite-time test for emptiness when $t$ is unknown.

The number $n$ may be zero, so $N=1$ and the address register then has its one-dimensional empty-word basis. The phase query is uncontrolled; no controlled-query capability is part of this definition.
alg-qa-11-grover-iterate:
## Definition

For a marked-search instance on $D_n$, let $|s\rangle=H^{\otimes n}|0^n\rangle=N^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in D_n}|x\rangle$ and $R_s=2|s\rangle\langle s|-I$. Prepare a response qubit from $|0\rangle$ by applying $X$ and then $H$, giving $|-\rangle$. Apply the standard bit query $U_f$ to the address and response registers; phase kickback applies $O_M$ to the address and leaves the response in $|-\rangle$. Then apply $R_s$ to the address register. This defines $G=R_sO_M$ with one standard bit query and no intermediate measurement. Repeated iterates reuse the response qubit in $|-\rangle$. The query count is separate from the preparation and reflection gate costs. A reflection about $|s\rangle$ may be represented as $H^{\otimes n}(2|0^n\rangle\langle0^n|-I)H^{\otimes n}$, whose reflection cost must be charged under the declared gate model.
lem-qa-11-good-bad-decomposition:
## Statement

Let $M\subseteq D_n$ have size $t$ with $0<t<N$. Define
$$|G\rangle=t^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in M}|x\rangle,\qquad |B\rangle=(N-t)^{-1/2}\sum_{x\notin M}|x\rangle.$$
Then $|G\rangle$ and $|B\rangle$ are orthonormal. For $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt{t/N}\in(0,\pi/2)$, the uniform state is
$$|s\rangle=\sin\theta\,|G\rangle+\cos\theta\,|B\rangle,$$
with $\sin^2\theta=t/N$.
thm-qa-11-grover-iterate-query-cost:
## Statement

One execution of [[alg-qa-11-grover-iterate]] makes exactly one standard bit-query call, through phase kickback. The response-qubit preparation and the reflection about $|s\rangle$ make no oracle calls and are charged separately as gates or explicitly supplied reflection operations.
alg-qa-11-known-count-grover-search:
## Definition

Input $N=2^n$, standard bit-query access to $f=1_M$, and the exact integer $t=|M|$. If $t=0$, return none without a query. If $t>0$, find $K$ as the least positive integer with $tK^2\ge N$: start with $\mathrm{lo}=0,\mathrm{hi}=1$, repeatedly set $\mathrm{lo}=\mathrm{hi},\mathrm{hi}=2\mathrm{hi}$ while $t\mathrm{hi}^2<N$, then use upper-midpoint binary search on the false/true interval until $\mathrm{hi}-\mathrm{lo}=1$. Thus $K=\mathrm{hi}=\lceil\sqrt{N/t}\rceil$. Prepare $|s\rangle=H^{\otimes n}|0^n\rangle$, set $q=1-2t/N$, and compute exactly the rational recurrence
$$T_0(q)=1,\qquad T_1(q)=q,\qquad T_{m+1}(q)=2qT_m(q)-T_{m-1}(q)\quad(1\le m\le2K).$$
Compute the recurrence through index $m=2K+1$. For each integer $k=0,\ldots,K$, compute $p_k=(1-T_{2k+1}(q))/2$. Choose the least $k$ attaining the maximum of this finite rational list, apply [[alg-qa-11-grover-iterate]] exactly $k$ times, measure the address register, and make one separate standard bit query to verify the candidate. Return the candidate if marked and the failure symbol otherwise. The state preparation, all-zero reflection, classical recurrence and comparison work, and oracle queries are distinct costs; this definition makes no polynomial-time preprocessing claim.
lem-qa-11-grover-invariant-plane-rotatio:
## Statement

Assume $0<t<N$ and use the orthonormal ordered basis $(|B\rangle,|G\rangle)$ of [[lem-qa-11-good-bad-decomposition]]. Let $\Pi_M$ project onto the marked-address span, $S_M=I-2\Pi_M$, and $R_s=2|s\rangle\langle s|-I$. The Grover iterate $G=R_sS_M$ preserves $\operatorname{span}\{|B\rangle,|G\rangle\}$, and in this basis has matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix}\cos(2\theta)&-\sin(2\theta)\\ \sin(2\theta)&\cos(2\theta)\end{pmatrix},\qquad \theta=\arcsin\sqrt{t/N}.$$
The initially prepared state has coordinate column $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)^{\mathsf T}$.
alg-qa-11-known-count-random-iteration-s:
## Definition

Input $N=2^n$, exact count $t$, and standard bit-query access to $f=1_M$. If $t=0$, return none without a query. If $t>N/2$, perform at most nine independent rounds: prepare a fresh address register by $H^{\otimes n}|0^n\rangle$, measure an address, make one standard bit query to verify it, and return it if marked; after nine failures return the failure symbol.

If $0<t\le N/2$, find the least positive integer $K$ satisfying $tK^2\ge N$ by binary search. Initialize $\mathrm{lo}=0$ and $\mathrm{hi}=2^{\lceil n/2\rceil}$; while $\mathrm{hi}-\mathrm{lo}>1$, put $\mathrm{mid}=\mathrm{lo}+\lceil(\mathrm{hi}-\mathrm{lo})/2\rceil$, replace $\mathrm{hi}$ by $\mathrm{mid}$ if $t\,\mathrm{mid}^2\ge N$, and otherwise replace $\mathrm{lo}$ by $\mathrm{mid}$. Set $b$ to the least nonnegative integer with $2^b\ge K$. In each of nine independent rounds, draw $b$ fair bits to obtain $j\in\{0,\ldots,2^b-1\}$. Reject the round without a query if $j\ge K$. Otherwise prepare a fresh $|s\rangle=H^{\otimes n}|0^n\rangle$ and a fresh response qubit $|-\rangle$ using $X$ then $H$, apply [[alg-qa-11-grover-iterate]] exactly $j$ times, measure the address register, and make one separate bit query to verify the measured candidate. Return it if marked. After nine unsuccessful rounds, return the failure symbol. Uniform-state preparation uses exactly $n$ Hadamards; each iterate uses one query and a separately charged reflection. No query, state-preparation, reflection-gate, or classical-bit cost is conflated.
alg-qa-11-bbht-unknown-count-search:
## Definition

Input $N=2^n$ and standard bit-query access to $f=1_M$, with no input giving $t=|M|$. Fix $c=3/2$ and initialize $\ell=0$. In each round increment $\ell$ and put $M_\ell=\lceil c^\ell\rceil$. First draw one uniform address $x\in D_n$ and verify it by one standard bit query; if $f(x)=1$, return $x$. Otherwise choose $j$ uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,M_\ell\}$, prepare a fresh address register as $|s\rangle=H^{\otimes n}|0^n\rangle$ and a fresh response qubit as $|-\rangle$ using $X$ then $H$, apply the Grover iterate exactly $j$ times, measure the address register, and verify the candidate by a separate standard bit query. Return a verified marked item and otherwise begin the next round. Every random choice and quantum register is fresh in each round. The algorithm has no false positive; when $t=0$ it continues forever and does not produce a finite-time emptiness decision. The gate and state-preparation costs are charged separately from the bit-query count.
thm-qa-11-exact-integer-iteration-formul:
## Statement

For $0<t<N$, let $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt{t/N}$. After an integer $k\ge0$ Grover iterates starting from $|s\rangle$, the probability of measuring a marked address is
$$p_k=\sin^2((2k+1)\theta).$$
For $t=0$ this probability is $0$, and for $t=N$ it is $1$ for every integer $k\ge0$; these endpoint cases are direct one-dimensional branches and do not normalize a nonexistent marked or unmarked state.
prop-qa-11-known-count-preprocessing-cos:
## Statement

For $t>0$, put $K=\lceil\sqrt{N/t}\rceil$ and $q=1-2t/N$. The exact selection procedure in [[alg-qa-11-known-count-grover-search]] computes the recurrence $T_0=1,T_1=q,T_{m+1}=2qT_m-T_{m-1}$ through $m=2K+1$ and compares $p_k=(1-T_{2k+1}(q))/2$ for $0\le k\le K$. If $n\ge1$, the recurrence numerators and denominators have $O(Kn)$ bits and schoolbook arithmetic selects the least maximizing $k$ in $O(K^2n^2)$ classical bit operations. For $n=0$, necessarily $N=t=1$ and the selection costs $O(1)$. Since $K=\Theta(\sqrt N)$ when $t=1$, the preprocessing can be exponential in $n$; this query bound supplies no end-to-end polynomial-time claim.
prop-qa-11-known-count-random-selection-:
## Statement

For $0<t\le N/2$, the procedure [[alg-qa-11-known-count-random-iteration-search]] computes $K=\lceil\sqrt{N/t}\rceil$ by $O(n)$ binary-search predicate evaluations on integers with $O(n)$ bits, costing $O(n^3)$ deterministic bit operations by schoolbook arithmetic. Computing $b$ and drawing the nine $b$-bit iteration labels uses $O(n)$ further classical bit operations and random bits. The direct-sampling branch $t>N/2$ uses $9n$ fair address bits and $O(n)$ classical bit operations for address and output bookkeeping. These bounds are for $n\ge1$; when $n=0$, only the direct branch occurs and its bookkeeping is constant. Quantum measurements, state preparation, gates, and oracle calls are separate costs.
prop-qa-11-known-count-random-gate-accou:
## Statement

Each uniform-state preparation uses exactly $n$ Hadamard gates. Write $R_0=2|0^n\rangle\langle0^n|-I$ and let $C(R_0)$ be its declared gate cost if implemented or supplied as a named reflection. Conjugation gives $R_s=H^{\otimes n}R_0H^{\otimes n}$, so an iterate uses $2n$ Hadamards, cost $C(R_0)$, and one bit-oracle query. For the $0<t\le N/2$ branch, the total nonoracle gate cost is at most
$$9\bigl[n+2+(K-1)(2n+C(R_0))\bigr],\qquad K=\lceil\sqrt{N/t}\rceil,$$
up to measurement and output handling. For $t>N/2$ it is at most $9n$ Hadamards plus measurement/output handling. The reflection is not a free oracle.
thm-qa-11-integer-iteration-regime:
## Statement

Put $a=t/N$ and $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt a$. If $0<a\le1/2$, some integer $k$ with $0\le k\le K=\lceil1/\sqrt a\rceil$ has
$$p_k=\sin^2((2k+1)\theta)\ge1-a.$$
If $1/2<a\le1$, $k=0$ lies in this range and $p_0=a>1/2$. The real-valued optimizer $k_*=\pi/(4\theta)-1/2$ is not in general an integer.
lem-qa-11-random-iteration-average:
## Statement

For $0<t\le N/2$, put $a=t/N$, $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt a$, and $K=\lceil1/\sqrt a\rceil$. If $J$ is uniform on $\{0,\ldots,K-1\}$, then
$$\mathbb E[\sin^2((2J+1)\theta)]=\frac12-\frac{\sin(4K\theta)}{4K\sin(2\theta)}\ge\frac14.$$
lem-qa-11-bbht-stage-success-bound:
## Statement

Let $0<a=t/N<3/4$, $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt a$, and let $J$ be uniform on $\{1,\ldots,M\}$. If the positive integer $M$ satisfies $M\ge4/\sqrt a$, then
$$\mathbb E[\sin^2((2J+1)\theta)]\ge\frac38.$$
thm-qa-11-bbht-termination-and-success:
## Statement

For $t>0$, the BBHT algorithm halts with probability $1$ and returns an element of $M$; the probability it has not returned a marked item after $r$ rounds tends to zero. For $t=0$, it never halts and never outputs an element.
thm-qa-11-known-count-success-bound:
## Statement

For exact known count $t>0$, the procedure [[alg-qa-11-known-count-grover-search]] outputs a marked item with probability at least $\max\{t/N,1-t/N\}$. It returns none with certainty when $t=0$ and returns a marked item with certainty when $t=N$.
thm-qa-11-known-count-random-success:
## Statement
 
For every exact known count $t>0$, the randomized known-count procedure returns a marked item with probability at least $2/3$. If $0<t\le N/2$, each round succeeds with probability at least $1/8$ and nine-round failure is at most $(7/8)^9<1/3$. If $t>N/2$, each direct-sampling round succeeds with probability greater than $1/2$, so nine-round failure is less than $1/512$. For $t=0$ the procedure returns none exactly.
thm-qa-11-bbht-expected-query-cost:
## Statement

For $t>0$, the BBHT algorithm has expected standard bit-query cost $O(\sqrt{N/t})$. The bound includes the direct membership test and a separate verification query in each attempted round, plus one query per Grover iterate through phase kickback. If $t=0$, it never halts and the expected query cost from finite execution prefixes is infinite.
thm-qa-11-known-count-query-cost:
## Statement
 
For $0<t\le N$, the exact known-count procedure uses $O(\sqrt{N/t})$ standard bit queries: one query for each Grover iterate and at most one separate verification query. If $t=0$ and the exact count is supplied, it returns none with no query. This is only a query bound; exact classical maximization can cost exponentially many bit operations in $n$.
thm-qa-11-known-count-random-query-cost:
## Statement
 
For $0<t\le N/2$, the nine-round randomized known-count procedure uses at most $9K=O(\sqrt{N/t})$ standard bit queries, where $K=\lceil\sqrt{N/t}\rceil$; rejected rounds use no oracle query and each accepted round uses $j\le K-1$ iterate queries plus one verification query. For $t>N/2$ it uses at most nine queries, and for $t=0$ it uses none. This is a query count only, not a gate or classical preprocessing bound.
